scope: Original optional figure-specific color treatments informed by a purposive 2026 paper study. These are not extracted author palettes, venue standards, defaults, or guaranteed accessibility schemes.
usage: Assign each actual scientific role before choosing hues. Select a family for its emphasis strategy, then inspect native and Office renders at final size. Existing approved references and themes remain unchanged.

soft-dual.purpose: Two peer modalities or model roles with a distinct shared interaction/objective.
soft-dual.treatment: Dark text on pale module surfaces. Saturated hues mainly on role glyphs, small tokens and selected relations. Keep phase headings neutral; use warm contrast for the shared mechanism.

plum-sage.purpose: Two persistent role families with a warm focal relation; useful when blue is already overloaded elsewhere in the manuscript.
plum-sage.treatment: Pale plum and sage support repeated role identity; amber marks the chosen focal relation. The purple family has no universal memory meaning. Keep text dark and do not imply frozen/trainable state from tint.

line-first.purpose: Simple control, state or memory relations where geometry and labels already carry the figure.
line-first.treatment: Mostly white/gray modules with dark ink. Assign the two accents to explicit relation types or states, with labels/dashes as redundant cues. Do not invent read/write or positive/negative semantics just to use both colors.

token-categorical.purpose: Several genuinely distinct token, context or representation categories that recur across stages.
token-categorical.treatment: Reserve category color for repeated small items and supply a local key or direct category labels. Do not color every surrounding module differently; token categories need explicit source meanings.
